newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - July 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - July 30.

text.p: These are significant items in the Ivorian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these items and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FRATERNITE MATIN

- Ivory Coast, keen to give oil, gas and minerals a greater role in its largely farm-based economy, hopes to start seismic onshore exploration in cooperation with China of southern coastal strip running from Aboisso to Sassandra next month, Mineral Resources and Oil Minister Lamine Fadika says in interview.
Others points included a restatement of plans:
* to boost off-shore oil and gas production
* for greater privatisation at national oil refiner SIR with government, which holds 47 percent of shares, planning to retain significant stake
* for opening of SIR capital to national and international investors as part of a $2 billion expansion plan for new refinery with annual capacity of 10 million tonnes of crude oil
Fadika says:
* government would consider lifting protection order on classified forest areas if mineral deposits there were on a world scale.
* Ivory Coast seeks to boost oil and mineral production so that sector contributes 25-30 percent of GDP by year 2005.
* Iron ore, nickel, bauxite, diamonds are potential growth areas

- European Union to help Ivory Coast's neighbours take part in its first international agricultural fair which is planned for November 28 to December 8 in commercial capital Abidjan; organisers say that companies starting to book stands at the fair, called SARA 97.
- Prime Minister Daniel Kablan Duncan opens new Japanese-funded fishing port in Ivory Coast's second port of San Pedro; says it will open way to associated processing industries
LA VOIE

- SYNAPOSTEL blue-collar trade union at privatised CI-TELCOM telephone company gives notice of one-day strike on August 4 over changes by the new French-led management to allowances and working conditions; second white-collar union urges staff to ignore strike call and support the new management.
- Police use tear gas to break up march by 70 civil servants made redundant in 1992 and still seeking compensation
LE JOUR

- Ivory Coast is number two supplier of mangoes to Europe after Brazil, producers and buyers association OCAB says; Ivorian mango exports have risen from 1,000 tonnes in 1990 to 8,500 tonnes in 1997. Season runs from March to June.
- Animals in Abidjan zoo lack an appropriate balanced diet because of budget problems, zoo director says
